spec_match.rationale: Implements the spec's own forms example — form:navigation-source and the submitter-button case — over a real GET form whose submission navigation is intercepted; two submit buttons make the submitter-specific matching observable.

interactive.rationale: Editable fields, two live submit buttons, a deliberately slow real submission navigation, aria-live status, and a submission log that timestamps start, mid-flight state and settle.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises form- and submitter-level matching with the pressed button spinning; the demo delivers and logs exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Distinguishes submitter from form and covers the no-selector tier via SubmitEvent.submitter fallback; Enter-key submission (implicit submitter) and POST-style submissions are not exercised.

references.rationale: chromestatus entry, spec section, and MDN SubmitEvent.submitter are linked.

conformance.rationale: Covered by the feature suite: parse probes, compound usage, idle invariant, and the manual mid-navigation contract that names this demo as a measuring instrument.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: autorun pressed Publish; the log recorded start (submitter=#publish), mid-flight pressed-button-busy=true with the other button idle, and settle; console clean; mobile emulation overflow-free. The native button:navigation-source path cannot run on 141 and is bannered; the autorun samples matches() so a 156 run verifies it directly.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts probe, fallback branch, per-submission completion, and the autorun submitter-only invariant (pressed busy AND other idle).

design_system.rationale: Variables only; the native busy state is emerald with black text (5.1:1), the fallback is amber dashed — distinct by design; button overrides set background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: Fieldset/legend, labelled inputs, focus-visible on all controls, aria-live status for submission progress and completion, and a role=log history.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360x740 DPR3: zero horizontal overflow, inputs full-width, buttons 44px, no console errors.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Don't disable submit buttons to block validation; do disable/mark busy after a valid submission is under way to prevent double-posts; keep name attributes and real submit buttons.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The form uses named controls and type=submit buttons; busy styling applies only while the submission's navigation is ongoing, and the note block quotes the double-submit guidance verbatim.

guidanceConsulted.query: show loading state on the link or submit button that started a navigation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Tie progress feedback to the initiating control.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Only the pressed submitter spins — natively via button:navigation-source, or via SubmitEvent.submitter in the labelled fallback.

openQuestions.title: Enter-key submission and the implicit submitter
openQuestions.detail: Submitting with Enter from the title field uses the form's default button as submitter. Verify on a 156 build whether button:navigation-source matches the default button in that case (SubmitEvent.submitter does), and add an Enter-path note to the page once observed.

summary: Practical form feedback: a slow intercepted GET submission where the form and only the pressed submit button show in-flight state. Chromium 141 CDP evidence covers the full fallback lifecycle with the submitter-only invariant asserted true and console clean; the native selector lane is honestly deferred to Chrome 156.
